Everything stays on this phone: a list of your photos and videos here (names, sizes, dates, dimensions), what you chose in Google Photos, how they match, a record of each copy with its check value, your settings, and an encrypted Google sign-in that is wiped when you disconnect. Nothing is sent anywhere except to Google, and only when you connect or copy.

Pomegranate shows where each photo lives (this phone, Google Photos, or both), copies what is only in Google Photos into a folder you choose, checks each copy, and then cuts its own access to Google so you can leave cleanly. It never deletes anything.

No data leaves this phone except requests to Google\'s sign-in and Photos Picker services, made only when you ask. There are no analytics, no crash reporting and no third-party services. Your Google access is revoked and all related data deleted when you disconnect.\n\nThe full policy is at giovf.github.io/pomegranate/privacy

resources.string: I have looked at the proof and my copies are where I want them
Your copies are saved inside a folder Google Photos usually backs up. Turn off backup for it (steps below) before deleting anything, or your copies may be uploaded again.
Tick the box above to unlock these steps.
Open the Google Photos app on this phone or photos.google.com on a computer.
Open Library, or search for a month or album you have checked.
Long-press one item, then drag or tap to select the rest. On a computer, click the first item, hold Shift and click the last.
Tap Delete (the bin) and confirm. Items go to Trash for 60 days.
To free the space now: Library → Trash → Empty trash.
In Google Photos, tap your profile picture → Photos settings.
Tap Backup and switch it off.
Alternatively keep backup on but open "Back up device folders" and switch off the folders you do not want uploaded, including the one your Pomegranate copies are in.
On a computer, also sign out of or uninstall any Google Photos uploader (such as Drive for desktop).
Turning off backup stops new uploads; it does not delete what is already there.
